symbols.name: input sequence
symbols.meaning: The sequence $x_0,\dots,x_{2r-1}$ of ring elements whose transform is taken.
symbols.quote: Let $x_0,\dots,x_{2r-1}$ be a sequence of ring elements; here $x$ names a sequence, not the formal variable of earlier pages.

symbols.name: input position
symbols.meaning: The position of an input entry $x_t$, running over $0,\dots,2r-1$.
symbols.quote: Let $t$ be the input position and $s$ the frequency index, $s=0,\dots,2r-1$.

symbols.name: frequency index
symbols.meaning: The index of a transform entry, running over $0,\dots,2r-1$.
symbols.quote: Let $t$ be the input position and $s$ the frequency index, $s=0,\dots,2r-1$.

symbols.name: transform of x
symbols.meaning: The transform entry at frequency $s$, the sum of $y^{st}x_t$ over the input positions $t$.
symbols.quote: Its transform has entries $\hat x_s=\sum_{t=0}^{2r-1} y^{st}x_t$.

symbols.name: frequency pair index
symbols.meaning: The index of the frequency pair $2i$ and $2i+1$, running over the $r$ pairs $0,\dots,r-1$.
symbols.quote: Write $i$ for the index of the pair of frequencies $2i$ and $2i+1$, so $i$ runs over $0,\dots,r-1$.

symbols.name: integer exponent
symbols.meaning: An integer exponent of $y$ in the inverse identity.
symbols.quote: where $u$ is an integer exponent of $y$ (here $u$ does not denote the butterfly input of earlier pages).

symbols.name: second sequence
symbols.meaning: The second sequence $z_0,\dots,z_{2r-1}$ of ring elements, transformed the same way as $x$.
symbols.quote: Let $z_0,\dots,z_{2r-1}$ be a second sequence of ring elements, with transform $\hat z_s=\sum_{q=0}^{2r-1} y^{sq}z_q$, where $q$ is the input position in $z$.

symbols.name: transform of z
symbols.meaning: The transform entry at frequency $s$ of $z$, the sum of $y^{sq}z_q$ over the input positions $q$.
symbols.quote: Let $z_0,\dots,z_{2r-1}$ be a second sequence of ring elements, with transform $\hat z_s=\sum_{q=0}^{2r-1} y^{sq}z_q$, where $q$ is the input position in $z$.

symbols.name: input position in z
symbols.meaning: The position of an entry $z_q$ of the second sequence, running over $0,\dots,2r-1$.
symbols.quote: Let $z_0,\dots,z_{2r-1}$ be a second sequence of ring elements, with transform $\hat z_s=\sum_{q=0}^{2r-1} y^{sq}z_q$, where $q$ is the input position in $z$.

symbols.name: output position
symbols.meaning: The position of an entry of the cyclic convolution, taken modulo $2r$.
symbols.quote: Let $x\ast z$ be the cyclic convolution of $x$ and $z$, with entries $(x\ast z)_h=\sum_{t+q\equiv h \pmod{2r}} x_tz_q$, where $h$ is the output position.

symbols.name: cyclic convolution
symbols.meaning: The cyclic convolution of $x$ and $z$, whose entries are $(x\ast z)_h$.
symbols.quote: Let $x\ast z$ be the cyclic convolution of $x$ and $z$, with entries $(x\ast z)_h=\sum_{t+q\equiv h \pmod{2r}} x_tz_q$, where $h$ is the output position.

relations.quote: It works in the [polynomial ring modulo yʳ + 1](polynomial-ring-y.md).
It is built on $y$ as a [primitive root of unity](roots-of-unity.md) of order $2r$: $y^r=-1$, so $y^{2r}=1$, and no smaller positive power of $y$ equals $1$.
A synthetic polynomial transform generalizes the [discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) to a polynomial ring whose roots of unity are powers of $y$.
